messages.subject: covariates in calculateDiffMeth
parts:
Hi All,
I have methylation data that shows clear donor effects when I cluster (PCA and cluster functions). is there a way to account for this in my DMR analysis? The manuscript suggests this is possible, but I cannot see how to add covariates to the calculateDiffMeth function.
thanks a lot
Liz

messages.author: ab8277113f65c05e
messages.subject: Re: covariates in calculateDiffMeth
parts:
Hi Liz,
See this thread about using covariates:
https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/methylkit_discussion/2OYTUbhvQNM

In your case, the following might work:
1) do PCA/SVD on percent methylation matrix
2) find the eigen vector that corresponds  to your effect/covariate
3) remove it from the eigen vector matrix by equalising it to zero, this should remove the donor the effect from your dataset
4) re-construct the % methylation matrix
5) using the original C+T counts and reconstructed % methylation values, calculate number of Cs and Ts and create a methylBase object, and do the test

Check the following to get insight on how to do these in R:
http://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Data_Mining_Algorithms_In_R/Dimensionality_Reduction/Singular_Value_Decomposition

If you need more help on this, I would need to see the data and for that you can contact me through my private e-mail.

Best,
Altuna
